Noto Sans Elymaic reads clean and modern, with open apertures and ascenders that barely rise above the x-height. Electroharmonix is the one built to be looked at, its broken-apart letters demanding attention, whereas Noto Sans Elymaic is built to be read.

Electroharmonix handles the striking part, splitting words into single letters, while Noto Sans Georgian keeps its short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies for the reading.

Electroharmonix is commanding, its words split into single letters by open gaps and its round characters drawn open-handed. And Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi gives the pair its best quality: strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark, with terminals cut back to leave a big gap.
